taxonomic_note: Stable species-level canonical entry; accepted local infraspecific concept S. drummondii var. texanum is taught internally.
look_here_first: Start with the lower leaves: in local var. texanum, broad serrate blades narrow into winged petioles, while tiny narrow leaves occur high on the flowering branches. Distal stems are densely hairy and widely spreading branches have densely short-bracted flower stalks. FNA var. texanum involucres typically 3.8–5.2 mm, heads bluish-white; compare glabrous stalks and 27–36 rays in S. eulae.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays Natural Purola flora records Symphyotrichum drummondii; Travis herbarium and Williamson county treatment document accepted var. texanum. Current Kew accepts S. drummondii var. texanum.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Exact county evidence; accepted local infraspecific concepts reconciled internally.

diagnostic_image_needs.role: Photograph a lower winged petiole and broad serrate blade WITH its stem
10× macro of dense distal stem hairs and very short peduncle bracts
Measured involucre 3.8–5.2 mm; whole branch architecture
Matched S. eulae glabrous peduncle and face-on ray count

comparisons.key_distinctions: Local var. texanum: hairy stems, winged lower petiole, 3.8–5.2 mm heads; Eulae: glabrous peduncles, 27–36 rays, hemispheric often 5–6.5 mm heads.
